name: Paasaal
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Seibert, Uwe. 2003. Review of: A grammar of Sisaala-Pasaale, by Stuart McGill, Samuel Fembeti and Mike Toupin (Language Monographs 4, Legon: IAS 1999). SIL Electronic Book Reviews 2003-014.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on stress; states 'Since the phonology of Pasaale was already described by Toupin 1995, the authors treat only morphology and syntax' and criticises the grammar for not marking tone. Establishes that the stress statement, if any, lives in Toupin 1995 (Collected Language Notes 22).

sources.citation: Moran, Steven. 2006. A grammatical sketch of Isaalo (Western Sisaala). MA thesis, Eastern Michigan University (commons.emich.edu/theses/73; GitHub copy) -- west2465, not paas1238; the source the earlier scan named.
sources.note: PDF saved but its text layer has no usable Unicode mapping (garbled); not scanned because it describes Western Sisaala (west2465), a different Glottolog language; Moran's 2009 expansion of the same description (readable) has no stress statement.

sources.citation: Jambadu, J. B. 2024. Compounding in Sisaali. MPhil thesis, University of Education, Winneba (data from Kpatoli, Pasaali and Gbieni dialects).
sources.note: Discusses stress only as the English compound-stress criterion (Chomsky & Halle, Plag examples); never applies it to Sisaali. States 'Sisaali is a tone language' (p.124) and defers tonal effects to future work. Silent on Sisaali word stress.

sources.citation: Mustapha, N. 2018. The morpho-syntax of the noun phrase in Sisaali. MPhil thesis, University of Ghana, Legon (Kpatolie south-western dialect).
sources.note: Sec. 1.2.3 gives vowels, consonants, ATR harmony and 'Sisaali is a tonal language' with lexical and grammatical tone; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Bushira, G. 2017. Some word formation processes in Sisaali. MPhil thesis, University of Education, Winneba (Tumulung dialect = Sisaala Tumulung [sil], not paas1238).
sources.note: Silent on stress; says tone distinguishes lexical items and grammatical meaning, 'Sisaali can be said to be a tone language' (p.2); reports Luri 2011 on syllable structure incl. Paasaali.

sources.citation: Dumah, Iren B. 2017. Question markers in Sisaali. MPhil thesis, University of Education, Winneba (data from the Paasaale dialect: Funsi, Kundugu, Yaala, Jumo, Buffiama).
sources.note: Silent on word stress (the two 'stressed' mentions are general typology from Ultan/Siemund and echo questions). Only prosodic statement: polar questions are coded by a high-low tone contour with lengthening on the final syllable of the phrase.

sources.citation: Moran, Steven. 2009 ms. Isaalo (Western Sisaala) grammar, work in progress (GitHub bambooforest/sisaala) -- west2465, not paas1238.
sources.note: Ch.2 phonology: 'Isaalo is a tone language... Tones may be high or low'; sec. 2.4 Tone (lexical and grammatical H vs L); no section or statement on stress/accent.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart. 2005. Sentence connectives and deictic shift in Paasaal narrative. Reading Working Papers in Linguistics 8: 119-147.
sources.note: Silent; only note: 'The Paasaal orthography (which is phonemic, but does not mark tone) is used throughout.'

sources.citation: Bendor-Samuel, John T. 1965. The Grusi sub-group of the Gur languages. Journal of West African Languages 2(1).
sources.note: Scan scanned at 300 dpi; lexicostatistical classification only (mentions Sisala dialects Isala, Gilbagale); nothing on tone or stress.
